source:
---
argmap-version: 0.3
title: "A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics (the Fields Medallists' declaration)"
author: "extraction round 1 (LLM-extracted from the declaration text, single elicitor)"
date: 2026-09-11
source: "Declaration of 25 Fields Medallists, posted with a preamble by Terence Tao as \"A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics\", What's new, 11 September 2026, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/a-severe-misalignment-of-ai-in-mathematics/ . Extracted from the post's text; the declaration's own signature page (linked from the post) was not consulted."
focus: [misaligned, urgent]
scope: >
  The whole declaration, nine paragraphs, plus Tao's preamble. Mapped: the
  two theses of paragraph 1 (the benchmark push is detrimental; the goals
  are misaligned), the proxy-versus-goal diagnosis of paragraph 5, the three
  concrete harms of paragraphs 5 and 6, the concession-and-however of
  paragraph 8, the generalization of paragraphs 4 and 7, and the closing
  ask of paragraph 9. Not mapped, as argumentatively inert: the signature
  list (it is the source's authority; a premise-less testimony line for it
  would count the authors' own belief a second time beside their argument),
  the Economist article, and the Leiden comparison in the preamble.
  Paragraphs 2 and 3 (what research mathematics is, what famous problems
  have been for) are the background the proxy claim rests on and live in
  that statement's gloss.
description: >
  Source-faithful extraction (D39 discipline): every number derives from the
  declaration's own wording via the R-STMT / R-STEP rubric in the comment
  block below, fixed before any value was assigned. Frontier roots carry
  register pairs from the register-to-pair table (D152; the class token sits
  in the trailing comment); every statement something concludes into carries
  a `# check:` interval at the source's register and no pin. All values keep
  the `?` marker, since the declaration states no number. Every strengthed
  line carries a `# kind:` key read off the source's connective. Quotes are
  verbatim spans with paragraph locators, ASCII-normalized in one respect:
  the source's curly quotation marks are transliterated.
---

# ============================================================
# SPINE. The declaration argues two theses in its first paragraph and
# generalizes them in its seventh:
#
#   @misaligned (the headline)  <- $misaligned-ev  (proxy vs goal, p5)
#                               <- $harm-ev        (the push is detrimental, p1)
#   @benchmark-harms (hub)      <- $goodhart-ev    (the tool turned against the goal, p5)
#                               <- three concrete harms, folded under it (p5, p6)
#                               <- the p8 concession, read as an answered objection
#   @broader                    <- $training-ev    (p7's general mechanism)
#                               <- $miniature-ev   (p4's analogy, via @misaligned)
#   @urgent (the ask)           <- $urgent-ev      (p9, with Tao's preamble)
#
# Shared grounds homed at document level, each with its consumers:
#   @companies-benchmark  - $misaligned-ev, $goodhart-ev, $fertile-ev
#   @proxy-not-goal       - $misaligned-ev, $goodhart-ev
#   @humans-decide        - $potential-resp (inside the harm hub), $urgent-ev
#   @capable              - $urgent-ev
# The two lines sharing @rushed inside the hub are two distinct consequences
# of one rush (attribution; the transmission chain); the shared premise is
# deliberate and is what makes them co-vary (D152 item 5).
#
# The one interpretive move: paragraph 8's "AI offers the potential ...
# However, whether these changes ultimately benefit the field ... will be
# determined by the decisions of the humans in control" is read as the
# authors' own concession answered by their own response (idiom 1), because
# the "However" marks the first sentence as the objection the second one
# meets. Everything else is transcription.
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# RUBRIC, fixed before any value was assigned (D36 rule 2). The register
# pairs follow the D152 register-to-pair table; the class token is in
# each root's trailing comment.
#
# R-STMT (the declaration's register for a statement -> marginal pair)
#   D-FLAT  flat indicative assertion ("is", "are", "has been",
#           "invariably", "must take care") .................. 0.85?/0.05?  (0.90, width 0.10)
#   D-LARGE "will in large part", "are becoming increasingly",
#           "offers the potential" ............................ 0.75?/0.05?  (0.85)
#   D-OFTEN "often" ........................................... 0.7?/0.1?    (0.80)
#   D-MANY  "in many ways" (a qualified likeness) ............. 0.55?/0.15?  (0.70)
#   derived statement (something concludes into it) ........... no pin; # check: at
#           the register's interval (D-FLAT: 0.85..0.95?)
#
# R-STEP (the register of an inference step -> strength)
#   unhedged asserted step ("is detrimental", "raises",
#           "cease to align", "must be addressed") ............ 0.85?
#   "would" conditional step .................................. 0.8?
#   response to an objection (role default) ................... 0.8?
#   two claims juxtaposed with no connective (role default) ... 0.7?
#   step carried by an analogy ("miniature version") .......... 0.6?
#   "may" / "could" hedged step ............................... 0.5?
#   an objection's own step (role default) .................... 0.5?
#
# Where two readings were defensible the weaker was authored and both are
# logged in the line's trailing comment.
# ============================================================


# ---- The headline and the hub ----

@misaligned [The goals of the AI companies and the goals of the mathematical community are severely misaligned]: the declaration's title claim, and the diagnosis its first paragraph reaches after calling the benchmark push detrimental. The signatories frame it as one instance of a wider misalignment between what AI is used for and what the work was for  # check: 0.85..0.95?  (D-FLAT)
  > The goals of the AI companies and the goals of the mathematical community are severely misaligned. [^p1]

$misaligned-ev [the companies optimize a proxy of the community's goal] 0.85? @misaligned | @proxy-not-goal AND @companies-benchmark: linked; the goals come apart exactly where one party pursues the proxy as its objective while the other pursues the thing the proxy stood for. Neither premise alone shows a misalignment: a benchmark is harmless where solving problems is the whole point, and the proxy observation is idle where nobody optimizes the proxy [^p5]  # kind: mechanism
$harm-ev [a push that damages the field it benchmarks on] 0.7? @misaligned | @benchmark-harms: the first paragraph puts the two claims side by side with no connective, so the step takes the juxtaposition default. A company whose chosen practice damages the science it draws on is pursuing something other than what the science pursues [^p1]  # kind: testimony

@benchmark-harms [The push by AI companies to solve mathematical problems as a benchmark is detrimental to mathematics as a science and as a community]: the hub of the case. What is at stake beyond mathematics itself is stated in paragraph 2: modern technologies and sciences are built on mathematical tools, so damage to the source shows up downstream  # check: 0.85..0.95?  (D-FLAT)
  > the push by AI companies to solve mathematical problems as a benchmark is detrimental to the science of mathematics, and to the mathematical community [^p1]

  # -- the three concrete harms (paragraphs 5 and 6). Convergent by the
  # source's own listing: three separate sentences, three separate damages.
  # $attribution-ev and $chain-ev share @rushed on purpose (see the spine
  # comment). --
  @rushed [AI solutions are often announced in a rush, with no proper writeup, no isolation of the new methods and no citation of the previous work of others] 0.7?/0.1?: the observation the two attribution and transmission harms rest on  # D-OFTEN
    > Often these solutions are announced in a rush, leaving no time for a proper writeup, the isolation of new methods and ideas, and citing relevant previous work of others. [^p6]
  @needs-integration [AI-conceived ideas become fully alive only through mathematicians who take care of their development and integration into the canon] 0.85?/0.05?: the claim about how an idea enters mathematics at all: through the long process of talks, discussions and simplifications that paragraph 3 describes, ending in a textbook presentation a student can study  # D-FLAT
    > without the willing mathematicians who must take care of their development and integration into the mathematical canon, AI-conceived ideas would never become fully alive [^p6]
  @slow-nurture [The community's most precious resources, students and ideas, grow only through processes that take time and rest on human interaction] 0.85?/0.05?: students are given problems chosen to develop their skills; ideas are disseminated in talks, private discussions and careful writeups that connect them to the previous ideas of others  # D-FLAT
    > These processes invariably take time and are based on human interaction. [^p4]
  $attribution-ev [a rush raises attribution and plagiarism questions] 0.85? @benchmark-harms | @rushed: the harm the declaration compares to every creative profession's [^p6]  # kind: mechanism
  $chain-ev [the transmission chain between mathematicians is lost] 0.8? @benchmark-harms | @rushed AND @needs-integration: linked; a rush is survivable where nothing needs integrating, and the need for integration is met where solutions arrive with careful writeups. Together they leave the integrators nothing to work with and no time to work in [^p6]  # kind: mechanism
    > the crucial human transmission chain between mathematicians would be lost [^p6]
  $fertile-ev [mass-produced true/false statements kill fertile ground] 0.5? @benchmark-harms | @companies-benchmark AND @slow-nurture: the "could" governs the step. Linked: a flood of settled statements is harmless where new ideas do not need slow ground to grow in, and slow ground is not threatened without the flood [^p5]  # kind: mechanism
    > the mass production at faster and faster pace of "true/false" statements could destroy fertile ground instead of breathing life into new ideas. [^p5]

  # -- paragraph 8's concession, read as an objection the authors answer
  # themselves (see the spine comment). The ground is theirs and takes its
  # own register; the objection step takes the role default. --
  @potential [AI offers the potential of enhancing and accelerating genuine mathematical study and understanding] 0.75?/0.05?: granted by the signatories without hedging on the potential itself; what they contest is whether it is realized  # D-LARGE
    > AI offers the potential of enhancing and accelerating genuine mathematical study and understanding. [^p8]
  $potential-obj [if AI can enhance the field, its push into it is no harm] 0.5? ~@benchmark-harms | @potential: the reading a reader of paragraph 8's first sentence would take away before the "However" [^p8]  # kind: hope
  $potential-resp [the potential is realized only by the right decisions] 0.8? @benchmark-harms | @humans-decide AND $potential-obj: the "However": a potential decides nothing by itself; the benchmark push as it stands is one set of decisions, and the declaration's whole point is that it is the wrong one [^p8]  # kind: mechanism

$goodhart-ev [optimizing the proxy turns the tool against the goal] 0.5? @benchmark-harms | @proxy-not-goal AND @companies-benchmark: the general mechanism of which the three folded harms are instances; "may" governs the step. Kept beside the instances because the source states it as its own sentence, and its low strength keeps the double count small [^p5]  # kind: mechanism
  > Forgetting this in the world of AI may turn the tool against the primary goal. [^p5]


# ---- Shared grounds, homed at document level ----

@capable [LLMs can now solve major outstanding problems in many fields of mathematics] 0.85?/0.05?: the premise everything else takes for granted; the declaration does not dispute the capability, it disputes what it is being used for  # D-FLAT
  > the mathematical capabilities of LLMs have improved dramatically, to the point that they can solve major outstanding problems in many fields of mathematics [^p1]
@companies-benchmark [AI companies push the solving of mathematical problems as a benchmark] 0.85?/0.05?: presupposed by paragraph 1's "the push by AI companies", and what paragraph 5 calls the mass production of true/false statements at a faster and faster pace  # D-FLAT
@proxy-not-goal [Solving problems is only a tool and a proxy for the primary goal of mathematics, which is conceptual understanding and insight] 0.85?/0.05?: the declaration's central distinction. Paragraphs 2 and 3 supply the background: research mathematics is the understanding of basic structures of shapes, numbers and natural phenomena, built over generations into a corpus of ideas, methods and abstractions; famous problems have served as landmarks and lighthouses against which improved understanding is measured, and solving one has been a sign of new insights and methods that the community then studies, simplifies and eventually turns into textbook material, some of it becoming, decades or centuries later, tools the whole population uses  # D-FLAT
  > solving problems is only a tool and proxy for achieving the primary goal of conceptual understanding and insight. [^p5]
  > Solving one of these problems has been a certain sign of new insights and interesting methods [^p3]
@humans-decide [Whether AI benefits or damages mathematics will in large part be determined by the decisions of the humans in control of the technology] 0.75?/0.05?: the profession will need to adapt in several ways, the signatories say, and yet the outcome is placed with the people who control the technology  # D-LARGE
  > whether these changes ultimately benefit the field or have a destructive effect will in large part be determined by the decisions of the humans in control of this new technology. [^p8]
@miniature [The mathematical community functions as a miniature version of humanity] 0.55?/0.15?: individuals using a wide variety of approaches, joined by core values; the likeness that lets the declaration read its own case as everyone's  # D-MANY
  > The mathematical community functions, in many ways, as a miniature version of humanity. [^p4]


# ---- The generalization and the ask ----

@broader [The same misalignment is a general threat to intellectual work beyond mathematics]: other scientific and creative professions face the issues now, the declaration says flatly; that all of humanity might face them is its hedged extension, carried in the gloss rather than in the label  # check: 0.85..0.95?  (D-FLAT, "We are witnessing a general threat")
  > We are witnessing a general threat to intellectual work, with misalignment between the outcome of the use of AI and its initial purpose. [^p7]
  @training-develops [Years of training have traditionally served not only to produce a final answer but to develop understanding and the ability to formulate new questions] 0.85?/0.05?: paragraph 7's premise about what the work was for  # D-FLAT
  @ai-direct [AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of producing the results of such work directly] 0.75?/0.05?: building on a vast body of previous human work  # D-LARGE
  $training-ev [a direct result decouples the work from its purpose] 0.85? @broader | @training-develops AND @ai-direct: linked; the goals only come apart where the process had a second purpose and the product can now be had without the process [^p7]  # kind: mechanism
    > these goals cease to align. [^p7]

$miniature-ev [what happens to a miniature happens to the whole] 0.6? @broader | @misaligned AND @miniature: the analogy step, at the analogy register; the source's own connective is that the community's issues "indicate issues that all of humanity might face", so the hedged reading (0.5?) was also defensible and the analogy default was kept because the professions claim beside it is flat [^p4] [^p7]  # kind: analogy

@urgent [These issues must be addressed urgently by the mathematical community, the AI companies and society]: the closing ask, and the reason Tao gives for releasing the statement without the consultative process the Leiden declaration had  # check: 0.85..0.95?  (D-FLAT, "must be addressed urgently")
  > These issues must be addressed urgently, in the mathematical community, by the companies developing these technologies and, more broadly, by a society that will confront similar problems in many other forms of intellectual work. [^p9]
  > we decided that the urgency of the situation was such that we needed to release a statement sooner rather than later. [^tao]

$urgent-ev [the harm is here now and its course is a human choice] 0.85? @urgent | @misaligned AND @humans-decide AND @capable: linked; a misalignment with no capability behind it could wait, a capability whose consequences nobody controls could not be addressed, and a human choice about a harmless technology needs no urgency. The declaration's addressees follow the three conjuncts: the community, the companies, and the society @broader says will meet the same problem [^p9] [^tao]  # kind: testimony


[^tao]: Terence Tao, "A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics," What's new, 11 September 2026, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/09/11/a-severe-misalignment-of-ai-in-mathematics/ : the preamble to the declaration.
[^p1]: The declaration, paragraph 1 (the summary: capabilities, the benchmark push, the misalignment, the broader issue), as posted on Tao's blog.
[^p3]: ibid., paragraph 3 (famous problems as landmarks and lighthouses; the long process from solution to textbook).
[^p4]: ibid., paragraph 4 (the community as a miniature of humanity; students and ideas as its resources).
[^p5]: ibid., paragraph 5 (solving problems as tool and proxy; the tool turned against the goal; fertile ground).
[^p6]: ibid., paragraph 6 (rushed announcements; attribution and plagiarism; the transmission chain).
[^p7]: ibid., paragraph 7 (the general threat to intellectual work; training and direct production; other professions and humanity).
[^p8]: ibid., paragraph 8 (the potential of AI; adaptation; the decisions of the humans in control).
[^p9]: ibid., paragraph 9 (the closing ask).
